topicName: Movement of Materials Into and Out of the Cell
description: This topic explains how substances such as gases, water and dissolved solutes move into and out of cells through diffusion, osmosis and active transport, and the factors and biological importance of these processes.

options.text: The movement of particles from a region of low concentration to a region of high concentration
The net movement of particles from a region of high concentration to a region of low concentration
The movement of water through a semi-permeable membrane only
The movement of particles using energy from respiration

mcq.explanation: Diffusion is the net movement of particles from where they are highly concentrated to where they are less concentrated, down a concentration gradient.

mcq.questionText: Osmosis is best described as the movement of water molecules from a region of:

options.text: Higher water concentration to lower water concentration through a semi-permeable membrane
Lower water concentration to higher water concentration through a semi-permeable membrane
Higher solute concentration to lower solute concentration
Any region to another using energy

mcq.explanation: Osmosis is the movement of water from a dilute solution (high water concentration) to a concentrated solution (low water concentration) across a semi-permeable membrane.

mcq.questionText: Which process requires energy in the form of ATP from respiration?

options.text: Diffusion
Osmosis
Active transport
Evaporation

mcq.explanation: Active transport moves substances against the concentration gradient and therefore needs energy supplied by ATP from respiration.

mcq.questionText: A type of membrane that allows only certain particles to pass through it is called a:

options.text: Permeable membrane
Impermeable membrane
Semi-permeable membrane
Cellulose wall

mcq.explanation: A semi-permeable (selectively permeable) membrane allows some substances such as water to pass but blocks others.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is an example of diffusion in living organisms?

options.text: Absorption of mineral salts by root hairs against a gradient
Exchange of oxygen and carbon dioxide in the lungs
Movement of water from soil into root cells
Uptake of glucose by cells against a gradient

mcq.explanation: Gas exchange in the lungs occurs by diffusion of oxygen and carbon dioxide down their concentration gradients.

mcq.questionText: When a plant cell is placed in pure water, it becomes firm and swollen. This condition is called:

options.text: Plasmolysis
Turgidity
Haemolysis
Flaccidity

mcq.explanation: Water enters the cell by osmosis, the cell swells and pushes against the cell wall, making it turgid.

mcq.questionText: A solution that has a higher solute concentration than the cell contents is described as:

options.text: Hypotonic
Isotonic
Hypertonic
Neutral

mcq.explanation: A hypertonic solution is more concentrated than the cell, so water leaves the cell by osmosis.

mcq.questionText: What happens to a red blood cell placed in distilled water?

options.text: It shrinks and crenates
It swells and bursts (haemolysis)
It becomes turgid without bursting
It remains unchanged

mcq.explanation: Water enters the red blood cell by osmosis; because it has no cell wall, it swells and bursts in a process called haemolysis.

mcq.questionText: Which factor does NOT increase the rate of diffusion?

options.text: A steeper concentration gradient
A higher temperature
A larger surface area
A thicker membrane

mcq.explanation: A thicker membrane increases the distance particles must travel, which slows diffusion rather than speeding it up.

mcq.questionText: In the visking (dialysis) tubing experiment, starch solution is placed inside the tubing and the tubing is placed in water with iodine. The water turns brown but stays brown while the contents inside turn blue-black only if starch could escape. What does this experiment mainly demonstrate?

options.text: That large starch molecules cannot pass through the semi-permeable tubing while smaller iodine molecules can
That all molecules pass freely through the tubing
That water cannot move through the tubing
That active transport is taking place

mcq.explanation: Visking tubing acts as a semi-permeable membrane: small iodine molecules diffuse in (turning starch blue-black) but large starch molecules cannot diffuse out.

mcq.questionText: The shrinking of the cytoplasm away from the cell wall when a plant cell loses water is called:

options.text: Turgor
Plasmolysis
Haemolysis
Diffusion

mcq.explanation: When placed in a hypertonic solution, water leaves the plant cell by osmosis and the cytoplasm and membrane pull away from the wall, a state called plasmolysis.

mcq.questionText: Root hair cells absorb mineral salts from the soil even when the salts are more concentrated inside the cell than in the soil. This is achieved by:

options.text: Diffusion
Osmosis
Active transport
Transpiration

mcq.explanation: Moving salts against their concentration gradient requires energy, so this is active transport.

mcq.questionText: Which of these is a biological importance of osmosis in plants?

options.text: Absorption of water from the soil by roots
Release of energy during respiration
Breakdown of food in the stomach
Formation of chlorophyll

mcq.explanation: Osmosis allows roots to absorb water from the soil and helps keep plant cells turgid, supporting the plant.

mcq.questionText: Two potato cylinders of equal size are placed in different solutions for one hour. Cylinder X gains mass and becomes firm while cylinder Y loses mass and becomes soft. What can be concluded?

options.text: X was in a hypertonic solution and Y in a hypotonic solution
X was in a dilute (hypotonic) solution and Y in a concentrated (hypertonic) solution
Both were in pure water
No osmosis occurred in either cylinder

mcq.explanation: X gained water by osmosis from a dilute solution, while Y lost water to a more concentrated solution outside the cells.

mcq.questionText: Which statement correctly compares diffusion and active transport?

options.text: Both move particles down the concentration gradient without energy
Diffusion needs energy while active transport does not
Diffusion moves particles down the gradient without energy, while active transport moves them up the gradient using energy
Both processes only move water molecules

mcq.explanation: Diffusion is passive and goes down the gradient, whereas active transport is energy-requiring and moves substances against the gradient.

fib.questionText: The net movement of particles from a region of high concentration to a region of low concentration is called _____.
fib.explanation: Diffusion occurs down a concentration gradient and does not require energy.

fib.questionText: The movement of water molecules across a semi-permeable membrane from a dilute to a concentrated solution is known as _____.
fib.explanation: Osmosis is essentially the diffusion of water through a selectively permeable membrane.

fib.questionText: The movement of substances against the concentration gradient using energy is called _____ transport.
fib.explanation: Active transport uses ATP energy from respiration to move particles up the gradient.

fib.questionText: A membrane that allows some substances to pass through but not others is described as _____.
fib.explanation: Semi-permeable (selectively permeable) membranes control what enters and leaves the cell.

fib.questionText: When a plant cell is full of water and firm, it is said to be _____.
fib.explanation: Turgidity gives support to soft plant tissues such as leaves and stems.

fib.questionText: The shrinking of the cytoplasm away from the cell wall when a plant cell loses water is called _____.
fib.explanation: Plasmolysis happens when a plant cell is placed in a hypertonic solution.

fib.questionText: The bursting of a red blood cell when too much water enters it by osmosis is known as _____.
fib.explanation: Red blood cells lack a cell wall, so they burst when they take in excess water.

fib.questionText: A solution that has the same solute concentration as the cell contents is described as _____.
fib.explanation: In an isotonic solution there is no net movement of water into or out of the cell.

fib.questionText: Increasing the _____ usually increases the rate of diffusion because particles move faster.
fib.explanation: Higher temperature gives particles more kinetic energy, speeding up diffusion.

fib.questionText: In experiments on osmosis, _____ tubing is often used because it acts as an artificial semi-permeable membrane.
fib.explanation: Visking (dialysis) tubing lets small molecules pass while holding back large ones.

tf.questionText: Diffusion requires energy from respiration to take place.
tf.explanation: Diffusion is a passive process and does not require energy.

tf.questionText: Osmosis is the movement of water molecules through a semi-permeable membrane.
tf.explanation: Osmosis specifically involves water moving across a selectively permeable membrane.

tf.questionText: Active transport can move substances from a low concentration to a high concentration.
tf.explanation: Active transport moves particles against the gradient using ATP energy.

tf.questionText: A plant cell placed in a concentrated sugar solution will become turgid.
tf.explanation: In a concentrated (hypertonic) solution water leaves the cell, so it becomes flaccid and may plasmolyse.

tf.questionText: The rate of diffusion increases when the concentration gradient is steeper.
tf.explanation: A larger difference in concentration speeds up the net movement of particles.

tf.questionText: Red blood cells have a cell wall that prevents them from bursting in pure water.
tf.explanation: Animal cells, including red blood cells, have no cell wall, so they can burst by haemolysis.

tf.questionText: Gas exchange in the alveoli of the lungs takes place mainly by diffusion.
tf.explanation: Oxygen and carbon dioxide diffuse across the thin alveolar walls down their gradients.

tf.questionText: A thicker membrane increases the rate of diffusion across it.
tf.explanation: A thicker membrane increases the diffusion distance and slows the process.

tf.questionText: In the visking tubing experiment, large starch molecules can easily pass out through the tubing.
tf.explanation: Starch molecules are too large to pass through the semi-permeable tubing.

tf.questionText: Turgidity caused by osmosis helps provide support to non-woody plants.
tf.explanation: Turgid cells press against their walls and keep soft tissues firm and upright.

summary.correctAnswer: The net movement of particles from a region of high concentration to a region of low concentration.
summary.explanation: It is a passive process driven by the concentration gradient and needs no energy.

summary.correctAnswer: The movement of water molecules from a dilute to a concentrated solution through a semi-permeable membrane.
summary.explanation: Osmosis is a special type of diffusion involving water only.

summary.correctAnswer: The movement of substances against the concentration gradient using energy from respiration.
summary.explanation: It allows cells to absorb substances even when they are more concentrated inside.

summary.questionText: Three main processes of moving materials into and out of cells
summary.explanation: Diffusion and osmosis are passive; active transport requires energy.

summary.questionText: Factors affecting the rate of diffusion
summary.correctAnswer: Concentration gradient, temperature, surface area, and thickness of the membrane.
summary.explanation: Steeper gradient, higher temperature and larger surface area speed it up; thicker membranes slow it.

summary.correctAnswer: A plant cell that is firm and swollen because it has taken in water by osmosis.
summary.explanation: Turgidity provides support to soft plant tissues.

summary.correctAnswer: The shrinking of the cytoplasm away from the cell wall when a plant cell loses water.
summary.explanation: It occurs when a plant cell is placed in a hypertonic solution.

summary.questionText: Importance of osmosis in living organisms
summary.correctAnswer: It enables roots to absorb water and keeps plant cells turgid for support.
summary.explanation: Osmosis is also vital for water balance in animal cells.

summary.questionText: Examples of active transport in organisms
summary.correctAnswer: Absorption of mineral salts by root hairs and reabsorption of glucose in the kidney.
summary.explanation: These move substances against their concentration gradients using energy.

summary.correctAnswer: It allows some substances to pass through while preventing others, controlling movement into and out of the cell.
summary.explanation: The cell membrane is selectively permeable and regulates exchange of materials.

hoq.questionText: A farmer adds too much fertiliser to the soil around his maize plants, and within a day the plants wilt even though the soil looks moist. What is the most likely explanation?

options.text: The fertiliser made the soil solution more concentrated than the root cells, so water left the roots by osmosis
The fertiliser blocked diffusion of oxygen into the leaves
The fertiliser increased active transport of water out of the soil
The fertiliser made the root cells turgid

hoq.explanation: Excess fertiliser makes the soil hypertonic, so water moves out of the root cells by osmosis and the plant wilts.

hoq.questionText: A student wraps fresh meat in salt to preserve it and notices liquid collecting around the meat after some hours. Which process best explains this and why does it help preservation?

options.text: Active transport pumps water out, killing bacteria with energy
Osmosis draws water out of the meat and out of microbes, making it hard for them to survive
Diffusion of salt into the air dries the meat
The salt increases the meat's turgidity, preventing decay

hoq.explanation: Salt creates a hypertonic environment, so water leaves the meat and any microbes by osmosis, slowing their growth and preserving the meat.

hoq.questionText: In an experiment, equal-sized potato cubes are left in salt solutions of increasing concentration. Predict how the change in mass of the cubes will vary as the salt concentration increases.

options.text: All cubes will gain the same mass regardless of concentration
Cubes will gain more mass as concentration increases
Cubes will gain mass in dilute solutions and lose mass in concentrated solutions, with greater loss at higher concentrations
Mass will not change in any solution because the cell wall blocks water

hoq.explanation: In dilute solutions water enters the cubes by osmosis (mass gain), but as the external solution becomes more concentrated water leaves the cubes, increasing the mass loss.
